articles.title: Jackson County Flood Warning and Dog Attack Charges
articles.body_md:
A flood warning remains in effect for the East Fork White River at Seymour, Jackson County, while two individuals have been charged with felony reckless homicide following a fatal dog attack in April 2025.

* Flood Warning remains in effect for East Fork White River at Seymour
* Two individuals charged with felony reckless homicide following fatal dog attack
* Infant died as result of the April 2025 dog attack

Heavy rainfall during the first half of last week produced minor flooding on the East Fork White River at Seymour.

Two individuals, including the infant's mother, were charged with felony reckless homicide for the fatal dog attack that occurred in Brownstown in April 2025.

The Jackson County Sheriff's Department has indicted Todd Banks, a 50-year-old resident of Brownstown, on one count of reckless homicide.
articles.blurb: A flood warning remains in effect for the East Fork White River at Seymour, Jackson County, while two individuals have been charged with felony reckless homicide following a fatal dog attack in April 2025.

articles.title: Sweet Scoop Market (Shell station, 2nd & Broadway)
articles.body_md:
# Facility audit & community review

Sweet Scoop Market at the Shell station on 2nd Street and Broadway in
Seymour, Indiana comes across as a dependable neighborhood business that
does the little things right. Posted hours: Monday through Saturday
6:00 AM to 11:00 PM, Sunday 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM â accessible for
commuters, evening travelers, and regular neighborhood traffic.

# Pricing

Very low prices on cigarettes, tobacco products, snacks, drinks, and
other convenience items. In a market where many stores are pushing
prices as high as they can, a place that stays competitive without
sacrificing service builds loyalty quickly. The Shell / Kroger
fuel-rewards integration adds real pump savings for regulars.

# Staff & management

Management is described by frequent customers as courteous and
welcoming; employees are friendly, efficient, and helpful during busy
times. Customer comments note that staff greet people genuinely, which
makes the stop feel more personal than a typical gas-station run.

# Community presence

- Part of daily routine for area residents
- Practical layout and quick service
- Clean, accessible, customer-focused
- Neighborhood sweet spot, not a cold chain stop

> Good prices alone don't create customer loyalty. People remember how
> they were treated. Sweet Scoop Market earns loyalty through
> courtesy, value, and consistency.

# Bottom line

One of the better gas-station markets in the Seymour area. Fair prices,
strong selection, welcoming service, dependable hours. Adds real value
to the neighborhood.
articles.blurb: Neighborhood Shell station market in Seymour run as a community-facing convenience stop. Frequent-customer audit: courteous management, low prices on tobacco and convenience items, solid fuel-rewards integration, consistent welcoming service.

articles.title: Payton Place Auto (Seymour / Columbus / North Vernon, IN)
articles.body_md:
# Executive overview

Payton Place Auto is a multi-location used vehicle dealer operating in
Seymour, Columbus, and North Vernon, Indiana, with the Columbus
location listed at 1021 25th St, Columbus, IN 47201. Public business
profile data shows the Columbus business started on June 6, 2017, is
organized as a corporation, and lists Clint Payton as president and
business management contact. The attached Facebook page screenshot
aligns with the Columbus location branding, address, category, phone
number, and a high visible recommendation score on Facebook,
indicating an active local social media presence tied to the business
identity shown publicly.

# Identity and footprint

The dealer's website presents Payton Place Auto as a used-vehicle
group serving Seymour, Columbus, and North Vernon, with the Columbus
store shown at 1021 25th St and a published store phone number of
(812) 413-5404. Third-party listings also connect the Columbus
operation to the same street address, though phone numbers vary across
platforms, including (812) 799-1601 on Yelp and Capital One Auto
Navigator, which suggests either multiple lines or inconsistent
directory maintenance. The Facebook page screenshot provided shows the
Columbus address, an (812) 657-1601 contact number, and describes the
business as locally owned, which further supports a real operating
presence but also highlights phone-number inconsistency across public
channels.

# Reputation signals

The strongest positive public-facing signal in the materials reviewed
is the Facebook page's visible "98% recommend (269 Reviews)" display.
Capital One Auto Navigator shows a 4.8 Google rating for Payton Place
Auto in Columbus, although the search result snippet does not include
the number of Google reviews, so this should be treated as a
directional reputation signal rather than a fully verified review
dataset. Yelp clearly shows the Columbus location exists and accepts
at least some customer interaction, but the surfaced Columbus result
snippet did not expose a rating total in the retrieved material,
limiting confidence in a full cross-platform reputation comparison.

# Business structure and credibility

BBB's business profile lists Payton Place Auto as a non-accredited
business with an A+ BBB rating, eight years in business, and a BBB
file opened on August 12, 2024. Non-accreditation is not itself
evidence of misconduct, but it means the business has not opted into
BBB accreditation standards and monitoring under that program. The
combination of a formal corporate listing, named management contact,
and multi-location website presence supports the conclusion that this
is an established local dealership group rather than a pop-up seller
or purely informal curb-lot operation.

# Friction points and risk flags

The clearest operational flag is inconsistent contact information
across official and third-party listings: the website and BBB show
(812) 413-5404, Yelp shows (812) 799-1601, Capital One shows
(812) 799-1601, and the Facebook screenshot shows (812) 657-1601. That
inconsistency does not prove wrongdoing, but it can complicate
customer follow-up, written quote validation, and complaint escalation
if a buyer later needs records tied to a specific salesperson or store
line. Another caution point is that reputation evidence available in
the retrieved public sources is mostly platform-level summary data,
not a fully sampled body of individual complaints and resolutions, so
a buyer should not rely on headline ratings alone.

# Legal and complaint review

No clearly surfaced public lawsuit or enforcement action specifically
tied to this Payton Place Auto operation appeared in the limited web
results reviewed here. Search results did surface unrelated Indiana
dealership enforcement coverage and older "Payton Wells" articles, but
those do not establish a direct connection to Payton Place Auto and
should not be conflated with this business absent documentary
evidence. Based on the sources gathered for this report, there is not
enough verified evidence to state that Payton Place Auto has a known
public enforcement history, but there is also not enough evidence here
to declare it unusually clean beyond the absence of surfaced hits.

# What a buyer should verify

Before publishing consumer-facing conclusions or making a purchase
recommendation, the most important next-step checks are practical
rather than speculative.

- Confirm which phone number is the primary service and sales contact
  for the Columbus store, and document that in writing.
- Request the buyer's order, financing worksheet, warranty terms, and
  all dealer add-ons before signing anything.
- Verify whether the advertised "3rd Party Inspections" claim on the
  Facebook page is standard practice for every vehicle or only
  available on request.
- Obtain a pre-purchase inspection from an independent mechanic and
  compare it against any dealer-provided inspection or reconditioning
  claims.
- Pull the vehicle history report independently rather than relying
  solely on dealer summaries.
- Confirm title status, open recalls, and whether any mandatory fees
  are excluded from online pricing.

# Publication-ready assessment

On the evidence reviewed, Payton Place Auto appears to be a real,
established independent used-car dealership group with a visible
Columbus storefront, multi-location website, named management, and
generally positive headline reputation signals on Facebook and
Google-adjacent listings. The main concerns are not overt scandal
indicators in the retrieved sources, but rather normal
independent-dealer diligence issues: inconsistent public contact data,
incomplete visibility into complaint resolution quality, and the need
to validate financing, inspection, and pricing details line by line.

A fair publishable characterization is that the business currently
presents as legitimate and locally established, but any customer
should still treat the transaction as a high-verification used-car
purchase rather than assuming headline ratings alone guarantee a
low-risk deal.

# Buyer protection one-pager

If you are about to buy from Payton Place Auto â or any independent
used lot in Indiana â do these eight things:

1. Confirm the salesperson's name, the store phone number, and the
   email â in writing â before you sign anything.
2. Pull the vehicle history report yourself (Carfax or AutoCheck);
   do not rely on the dealer's printout alone.
3. Pay an independent mechanic to do a pre-purchase inspection.
4. Read the buyer's order line-by-line. Refuse to sign with blank
   fields. Add-on packages, warranty admin fees, and "doc fees" are
   where surprise costs hide.
5. Ask for the warranty terms in writing â including who pays the
   repair shop and how the dealer responds if a covered failure
   occurs the day after delivery.
6. Confirm the title is clean, the open-recall list is empty, and the
   odometer disclosure matches the title document.
7. Photograph the car and the lot's posted price tag before signing.
8. Save every text message and email exchange. If something goes
   wrong, those records are your evidence.
articles.blurb: Multi-location independent used-vehicle dealer with an A+ but non-accredited BBB profile, mixed cross-platform reviews, and inconsistent contact information across listings. Published as a buyer due-diligence reference.

articles.title: Flock Safety ALPR network â Seymour, IN deployment
articles.body_md:
# Why this finding exists

Flock Safety automated license plate readers (ALPRs) are camera systems
that photograph every vehicle that passes them, run the license plate
against a hot list, and store the read for downstream search. Direct
observation in Seymour, Indiana suggests a dense concentration of
these cameras around a local mobile-home park â the kind of pattern
civil-liberties groups have flagged elsewhere as a red flag for
disproportionate, lower-income-targeted surveillance.

# What is a Flock camera

A Flock camera is a small solar-powered pole-mounted ALPR. It records:

- the license plate of every passing vehicle
- the vehicle make/model/color (via on-device computer vision)
- date, time, lane, direction
- a still image of the vehicle

Reads are uploaded to Flock's cloud and made searchable by the
contracting agency (in this case, Seymour Police Department). Through
"law-enforcement information sharing," reads have historically been
searchable by other agencies â including, in documented cases, U.S.
Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

# What we observed in Seymour

Multiple Flock cameras appear to be deployed in a tight cluster around
a mobile-home park in Seymour. The same observation, repeated by
other residents, is the trigger for opening this finding.

# What public records will close the case

- Seymour Common Council meeting minutes covering the Flock contract
- The Flock Safety transparency portal for Seymour PD
- Indiana APRA requests for the Flock contract, hot-list policy, and
  data-sharing settings
- DeFlock.me crowdsourced ALPR coordinates for Seymour

# How to access cameras and signals

**Legal access options.** Flock Safety leases solar-powered LPR cameras
to law enforcement, neighborhoods, and businesses. Public access to
live feeds is restricted; FlockOS access requires being an approved
customer.

**Locating cameras.** DeFlock.me publishes crowdsourced Flock camera
locations on OpenStreetMap. EFF's Atlas of Surveillance tracks
deployments by agency. Cameras are typically pole-mounted with solar
panels.

**Detecting signals.** Flock cameras emit BLE signals for networking;
open-source projects on GitHub use ESP32 hardware to passively detect
them. Researchers have demonstrated RF leakage in the 592â594 MHz
range from internal modules â interceptable with software-defined
radios within a few meters.

**Legal warning.** Intercepting feeds or signals without authorization
violates wiretap and computer-fraud statutes. Stick to public maps and
official channels.

# The civil-liberties context

Independent reporting from the ACLU, Electronic Frontier Foundation,
404 Media, The Markup, Wired, and Forbes has documented:

- ALPR data being searched outside the originating agency's stated policy
- Federal access to local ALPR data, including by ICE
- Concentration of Flock deployments in lower-income, majority-minority,
  and mobile-home neighborhoods
- Wrongful-stop incidents from misread plates or stale hot-list entries

# What you can do

- If you live near or in the trailer park described above and you have
  a photo of a pole-mounted ALPR camera you can timestamp, submit a
  tip via the IBE tip form.
- If you sit on the Seymour Common Council, a copy of the Flock
  contract and the deployment-location list closes the question of
  camera count and placement.
- If you are with a Seymour-area civil-liberties organization, the
  APRA request paths above are open, and we will publish the
  responsive records here in full.

# Caveats and standing notes

- This finding is open. It will be updated as observations are added
  and records arrive.
- We will not publish exact GPS coordinates until placements are
  verified by direct observation (timestamped) or a public record.
- Critique of a deployment pattern is not a critique of any individual
  Seymour PD officer or employee.
- Tip submitters are confidential by default.

> *Surveillance is not neutral. Where the cameras go, who they watch,
> and how the data is shared are policy decisions. Decisions deserve
> daylight.*
articles.blurb: Direct observation suggests a dense cluster of Flock Safety license plate readers around a Seymour mobile-home park. Documents the pattern, the access/detection landscape, and lists the public records that will resolve the question.

Electronic Frontier Foundation â ALPR coverage
